narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 59% probability that you would be a bad credit risk—meaning that, based on the information reviewed, you were somewhat more likely than not to struggle with repayment. The strongest factor was your checking account position: having a balance between 0 and 200 DM pushed the decision toward bad credit, and this was the most influential issue. Most approved applicants had no balance recorded. Your credit history—showing critical or other credits—was the second most influential factor, but it actually worked in your favor by offsetting some risk. The third factor was an existing bank installment plan, which pushed toward bad credit; approved applicants much more often had no such plan, about 87% versus under 9%. Other details, such as requesting 24 months when approved applicants average about 19, and having two existing credits when the approved average is about 1.4, reinforced the cautious view but ranked below the top three. To improve your chances, reduce or clear any overdraft or checking balance, avoid adding bank installment plans, and lower existing credit commitments before reapplying. You may also ask the lender what specific records were used and whether a guarantor or a smaller, shorter loan would be considered.
